verdict.line: You lose if you stand in Q (Ntofo Strikes) stack range and let him hit two for the pull-in shockwave, but you win long trades once E (Enrage) is active and his W (Path Maker) is down.

brief.thesis: K'Sante holds the measured lane and solo-kill edge because his Q (Ntofo Strikes) pokes you for free every 3.5 seconds and stacks toward a shockwave pull, but Sion's 52.8% head-to-head over 72 games says the matchup swings back once you play around his cooldowns instead of his stats. His real power is burst windows tied to W (Path Maker) and R (All Out); outside those windows he's just trading autos into your shield and passive.

theirWindow.when: he has 2 Q stacks and W up
theirWindow.what: He can fire the Q (Ntofo Strikes) shockwave to pull you in, then follow with W (Path Maker) for the knockback stun. Do not sit in his Q range while he's holding a second stack; back off a step until it falls off.

yourWindow.when: his W (Path Maker) is on cooldown (14-10s)
yourWindow.what: Engage with Q (Cryptic Gaze) to stun him from 550 range, then full-commit autos with E (Enrage) active. Without W he has no stun or reduced-damage window to punish your all-in.

start.why: Flat damage reduction on hit directly negates his Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke pattern, which is 51.2% of starts and the stronger winrate (43.2% over 44 games) into an early poke matchup like this one.

boots.why: 51.1% winrate and 57% pick rate; the flat physical damage reduction on autos directly blunts his Q poke and auto trades, which matter more than the speed from Swiftness here.

core.why: Stacks health from autos, which synergizes with E (Enrage) converting that health into attack damage every trade.
Core second item in the top build path (7.9% pick), gives sustain and damage reduction that lets you out-heal his Q poke into sustained trades.
100% winrate over 3 games in this exact third-item slot; passive burn adds pressure while you tank his engages.

runes.keystoneWhy: Heals you every 4 seconds on an enemy hit, directly countering his Q (Ntofo Strikes) chip damage and letting you win the extended poke war instead of just surviving it.

summoners.why: 92% pick rate and the highest winrate (53.8%) pairing; Teleport lets you reset after losing the early poke exchanges without giving up wave presence, and Flash covers his W (Path Maker) stun setups.

playing.title: Hold E off until engage
playing.detail: E (Enrage) has no cooldown but burns your health per attack, so only toggle it on right before your all-in window, not during passive poke exchanges where you're just losing health to his Q for free.

playing.title: Count his Q stacks
playing.detail: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes he fires a shockwave that pulls you in. Step out of his 450 range the moment you see the second stack land instead of waiting to get yanked.

playing.title: Punish dead W cooldown
playing.detail: W (Path Maker) is 14 seconds at rank 1 down to 10 at rank 5. Track when he's used it recently; that's your window to walk up and Q (Cryptic Gaze) stun him from 550 range without fear of his knockback stun.

playing.title: Save R for extended fights
playing.detail: R (Cannibalism) is a 90-second cooldown lifesteal-and-allies-heal effect, not burst damage. Pop it when you're committing to a long trade or skirmish, not as a panic button in a short poke exchange.

playing.title: Respect level 11-15 All Out spikes
playing.detail: Once he hits R (All Out), his abilities transform and he gains damage, healing, and speed at the cost of defenses. Fight him before he pops it or burn his shield (Footwork) and dash cooldowns first so he can't chain into the transform safely.

playing.title: Shield-tank the poke, don't facecheck
playing.detail: W (Death's Caress) absorbs damage before it explodes outward; pop it proactively when you expect his Q poke rather than reactively, since it doesn't come free (8s cooldown) and timing it wrong wastes the shield.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, boots, and summoner picks above are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the win-condition reads, cooldown timings, and trade-window calls are my own tactical analysis layered on top of that data.
